thesis.core: Construction Bank is a profitable, well-capitalized systemic bank with H1 2026 net interest margin stabilization and modestly improving reported asset quality. However, risk-weighted asset growth reduced CET1 by 39bp, while the October price rally leaves insufficient capital appreciation versus the current 10% new-capital hurdle.
thesis.variant_wedge: Price strength is supported by a stable banking franchise, not an earnings breakout. H1 attributable profit growth of 4.62%, 1.37% NIM and 9.52% annualized ROE justify a reasonable PB, but do not by themselves justify paying materially above normalized book value.
thesis.normalized_earnings_basis: Use 2026H1 common BVPS RMB13.69 and annualized reported ROE 9.52% to underwrite sustainable capital generation. FY normalized EPS cross-check approximately RMB1.30 from 2026H1 EPS RMB0.65 times two; not a mechanical forecast or valuation anchor.

operating_and_financial_quality.judgment: Franchise and capital buffers pass the fundamental quality gate. Risks: CET1 fell 39bp from year-end as RWA expanded; NIM remains low despite stabilization; credit risk is cyclical. Proposed H1 dividend requires final approval/implementation and is not counted as realized total return.

normalized_earnings_basis.rationale: P/B is primary because bank capital, asset quality and sustainable ROE are observable; price-target expected return excludes future dividends and prospective BVPS growth to avoid unsupported optimism.

catalysts: 2026Q3 report confirms stable or improving NIM without adverse credit migration.
Core Tier-1 capital ratio stabilizes or rebuilds while maintaining prudent credit growth.
Sustainable common dividends are approved and implemented without capital dilution.
Deposit funding costs fall faster than asset yields and fee income remains resilient.
kill_thesis: NPL formation and credit costs accelerate or provision coverage materially weakens.
Core Tier-1 capital falls persistently despite retained earnings, limiting dividends or growth.
Net interest margin resumes structural compression with no cost/fee offsets.
New capital issuance or regulatory requirements materially dilute common shareholder economics.
